nodes.label: Build for production scale rules
nodes.rationale: The system is treated as production holding terabytes of documents and millions of orders with many concurrent users; the current setup is sized for the demo corpus but code must not assume data stays small.

nodes.label: Incremental and idempotent indexing
nodes.rationale: Re-index only changed files (content hash / mtime), make every job safe to retry, and design it to run as per-file jobs on a queue.

nodes.label: Keep backends behind interfaces
nodes.rationale: Vector store, keyword index, cache, rate limiter, database and LLM are each accessed through one module so swapping Chroma for pgvector is a config change, not a rewrite.

nodes.label: Bound everything (row limits, timeouts, token budgets, step caps)

nodes.label: Stateless app processes
nodes.rationale: No per-process state that must be shared across instances (cache, rate limits, sessions); put it behind an interface that can move to Redis.

nodes.label: Security is enforced outside the model
nodes.rationale: Access filtering, the SQL guard, role views and read-only connections stay in code and the database, never in the prompt. The model never supplies user identity.
nodes.norm_label: security is enforced outside the model

nodes.label: Ingest pipeline (local, no API calls)
nodes.rationale: discover_files, file_hash + CHUNKER_VERSION vs manifest.json to skip unchanged files, load_file, split_documents at headings then 1000-char windows prefixed with section path, ACL group tags, local MiniLM embeddings into Chroma + SQLite FTS5, heartbeat written to indexer_status.json.

nodes.rationale: answer_question() is the single entry point for both the CLI and web UI, so guardrails apply everywhere by construction.
nodes.norm_label: answer_question() as single guardrail entry point

nodes.label: Hybrid retrieval: vector + BM25 fused with RRF (EnsembleRetriever)
nodes.rationale: BM25 uses a custom regex tokenizer because the default splits on whitespace, making a whole URL one unmatchable token.
nodes.norm_label: hybrid retrieval: vector + bm25 fused with rrf (ensembleretriever)

nodes.label: Adaptive retrieval breadth (compute_k)
nodes.rationale: k is derived from corpus size (about +1 per 100 chunks, clamped 4-20, override RAG_RETRIEVAL_K). A fixed k=4 was fine at 54 chunks but silently starved recall at 1,038 chunks. Wider retrieval raised cost (~$0.011 to ~$0.020) until the reranker and Haiku grading trimmed what reaches Sonnet (about $0.0055 per answered question on the fixture golden set).

nodes.label: Haiku relevance grading (fails open, rewrite and retry once)
nodes.rationale: A grading error keeps every chunk: grading trims cost and noise, it never authorizes.
nodes.norm_label: haiku relevance grading (fails open, rewrite and retry once)

nodes.label: Answer cache (per user + question + index version, first turn only)
nodes.rationale: A hit re-runs the access check on every source file, so revoked permissions turn it into a miss.
nodes.norm_label: answer cache (per user + question + index version, first turn only)

nodes.label: Prompt-injection resistance (retrieved_context tags as untrusted data)
nodes.norm_label: prompt-injection resistance (retrieved_context tags as untrusted data)

nodes.label: Per-file NAS access check (query-time, as the asking user)
nodes.rationale: Every retrieved chunk's file is opened over SMB as the asking user before generation; revoking NAS access takes effect on the next question with no reindex.
nodes.norm_label: per-file nas access check (query-time, as the asking user)

nodes.label: Two-stage authorization (index-time tags + query-time check)
nodes.rationale: Index-time group tags are a cheap pre-filter but a stale snapshot; the query-time SMB open is authoritative. There is no user table or group file; login opens a real SMB session. Retrieval over-fetches (RAG_OVER_FETCH 3x) so filtering leaves enough context. A fully-filtered result uses the same wording as an empty one so a refusal never reveals a document exists.

nodes.label: Secret redaction and streaming redaction
nodes.rationale: Narrow high-precision patterns only, since a generic long-number pattern would false-positive on medical record IDs and phone numbers. Streaming holds back the newest 80 characters so a secret split across chunks is never on screen.

nodes.label: Source attribution via sources_used structured output
nodes.rationale: A plain text-instruction version was tried first and proved unreliable (the model dropped it on longer answers), so sources_used is a schema field validated against what was retrieved.
nodes.norm_label: source attribution via sources_used structured output

nodes.label: Rate limiting (30 questions/hour per session, in-memory)
nodes.norm_label: rate limiting (30 questions/hour per session, in-memory)

nodes.label: JSON event logging (logs/events.jsonl)
nodes.rationale: Source paths are logged, never chunk text, because the log file is not access-controlled. cost_usd is null (never silently zero) when a model is absent from PRICING. Token counts include the query-rewrite call.

nodes.label: Golden-set evals (retrieval-only and --live with LLM judge)
nodes.rationale: Live eval runs with the answer cache off so a cached answer can't hide a regression; agent cases are checked on outcomes, never on the order of steps.
nodes.norm_label: golden-set evals (retrieval-only and --live with llm judge)

nodes.label: Why both tests and evals
nodes.rationale: A hybrid retriever is deliberately redundant: when BM25 degrades, vector search still surfaces the right chunk. A deliberately broken _tokenize() passed the full retrieval eval while tests/test_units.py caught it. Evals cover the pipeline end to end; unit tests guard components the pipeline can mask.

nodes.label: Four modes (orders, agent, content, find a file)
nodes.norm_label: four modes (orders, agent, content, find a file)

nodes.label: Ask about orders mode (NL to SQL with guard)
nodes.rationale: Claude writes the SQL; search/orders.py runs it only if it is a single SELECT over the asker's role views, read-only, LIMIT 50, 2s timeout.
nodes.norm_label: ask about orders mode (nl to sql with guard)

nodes.label: Ask the agent mode (bounded tool loop, five tools)
nodes.rationale: Tools: search_docs, query_orders, find_file, ask_user, final_answer. Same guards inside the tools; role and access check bound in code, no tool takes identity as an argument. Bounded by RAG_AGENT_MAX_STEPS (6), a token budget and a deadline. Ungrounded answers are replaced and uncited files dropped. Opt-in because it makes several model calls per question.
nodes.norm_label: ask the agent mode (bounded tool loop, five tools)

nodes.label: Find a file mode (SQLite FTS5 over names and paths)
nodes.rationale: Costs nothing per query and covers files whose contents are never indexed (images, drawings, archives), which on a disorganized share is most of them.
nodes.norm_label: find a file mode (sqlite fts5 over names and paths)

nodes.label: Ingest in CI (Python) / query in browser (JavaScript) split
nodes.rationale: Ingest runs once per deploy in CI with the real Python pipeline; the query path runs per question in the browser, so there is no server, no API key and nothing billable.
nodes.norm_label: ingest in ci (python) / query in browser (javascript) split

nodes.label: index.json hand-off (chunks, embeddings, pipeline constants)
nodes.rationale: Pipeline constants (k, fusion constant, rerank top-N, score cutoff) are read from the Python source so the two halves never hold different numbers.

nodes.source_location: The query path, step by step
nodes.rationale: Uses all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 via Transformers.js; BM25 uses the same tokenizer and constants as the Python FTS5 index; cutoff of -6 was calibrated on this corpus (answers score about -4 to +8, unrelated about -11).
nodes.norm_label: browser query path (embed, meaning search, bm25, rrf, rerank, cutoff)

nodes.label: Search as role switch (Admin / Engineer / HR / Contractor)
nodes.rationale: search.js drops files a role cannot open before retrieval, as the Python group filter does; a blocked file gets the same 'not covered' message as a missing one so its existence does not leak.
nodes.norm_label: search as role switch (admin / engineer / hr / contractor)

nodes.label: Where company search breaks (live failure cases)
nodes.rationale: The 'What just happened' text is computed from each run's actual rankings, never written in advance.

nodes.norm_label: pipeline x-ray (four ranked lists side by side)

nodes.label: Requests since the models loaded (PerformanceObserver privacy meter)
nodes.norm_label: requests since the models loaded (performanceobserver privacy meter)

nodes.label: Orders pattern translator (nine parameterized SQL templates)
nodes.rationale: With no language model, the question is matched to one of nine query types by embedding similarity and values fill a parameterized template, so nothing typed becomes SQL text. Below similarity 0.45 it declines rather than guess. 'My orders' asks which customer rather than matching the nearest list.
nodes.norm_label: orders pattern translator (nine parameterized sql templates)

nodes.label: Per-role SQL views (prices hidden, West region only, no access)
nodes.norm_label: per-role sql views (prices hidden, west region only, no access)

nodes.label: Demo agent chat panel (docked bottom-right, own role switch)
nodes.rationale: The page calls no model, so a question with a saved run replays it and any other question runs live with fixed steps. The panel's role switch is separate from the page's 'Search as'.
nodes.norm_label: demo agent chat panel (docked bottom-right, own role switch)

nodes.label: Back-and-forth rule (short reply joined to the asked-back question)
nodes.rationale: A reply of at most 8 words that is not itself a question completes the question the agent asked back about; that is the only context carried between messages since there is no model.
nodes.norm_label: back-and-forth rule (short reply joined to the asked-back question)

nodes.label: Live runs (liverun.js: SQL templates then policy search, no model)
nodes.rationale: The answer is the translator's sentence plus the top passage of each search (at most 3 hold-reason searches), so it says nothing the steps did not return.
nodes.norm_label: live runs (liverun.js: sql templates then policy search, no model)

nodes.label: Saved agent runs (agent.json built by agent_runs.py, scripted by agent_examples.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Tools, guards, role views and retrieval are real; only the model's step choice and answer wording are scripted. The build fails if a scripted answer claims more than its steps returned or holds something its role may not see. The --live path that records the real agent has not been run yet.
nodes.norm_label: saved agent runs (agent.json built by agent_runs.py, scripted by agent_examples.yaml)

nodes.label: Staleness fingerprint (agent_runs.py --check)
nodes.rationale: agent.json stores a fingerprint of fixtures, prompts, tool definitions, model, questions, roles and example script, recomputed on every deploy with no API call.

nodes.label: Typed question matching (0.8 similarity + matching numbers)
nodes.rationale: Rewordings scored 0.60-0.93 and look-alikes up to 0.77, so no threshold separates them; the page uses 0.8 and also requires numbers in both questions to match, and one order never matches many. 8 of 14 test rewordings match a saved run; the rest run live.
nodes.norm_label: typed question matching (0.8 similarity + matching numbers)

nodes.label: Demo roles are an illustration, not security
nodes.rationale: On a static page every run ships with the page, so the role switch only replays the run made for that role; real enforcement lives in the full app's database and file server.
nodes.norm_label: demo roles are an illustration, not security
